abducens_nerve_vi_left.name: Abducens nerve (VI) (left)
abducens_nerve_vi_left.description: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze. It is a somatic efferent nerve.

abducens_nerve_vi_right.name: Abducens nerve (VI) (right)
abducens_nerve_vi_right.description: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze. It is a somatic efferent nerve.

accessory_branch_of_middle_meningeal_art.name: Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery (left)
Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery (right)

accessory_nucleus_of_oculomotor_nerve_le.name: Accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve (left)
accessory_nucleus_of_oculomotor_nerve_le.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

accessory_nucleus_of_oculomotor_nerve_ri.name: Accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve (right)
accessory_nucleus_of_oculomotor_nerve_ri.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

adenohypophysis.name: Adenohypophysis
adenohypophysis.description: A major organ of the endocrine system, the anterior pituitary (also called the adenohypophysis or pars anterior) is the glandular, anterior lobe that together with the posterior lobe (posterior pituitary, or the neurohypophysis) makes up the pituitary gland (hypophysis).

amygdaloid_body_left.name: Amygdaloid body (left)
amygdaloid_body_left.description: The amygdala (; plural: amygdalae or amygdalas; also corpus amygdaloideum; Latin from Greek, ἀμυγδαλή, amygdalē, 'almond', 'tonsil') is one of two almond-shaped clusters of nuclei located deep and medially within the temporal lobes of the brain's cerebrum in complex vertebrates, including humans.

amygdaloid_body_right.name: Amygdaloid body (right)
amygdaloid_body_right.description: The amygdala (; plural: amygdalae or amygdalas; also corpus amygdaloideum; Latin from Greek, ἀμυγδαλή, amygdalē, 'almond', 'tonsil') is one of two almond-shaped clusters of nuclei located deep and medially within the temporal lobes of the brain's cerebrum in complex vertebrates, including humans.

angular_artery_left.name: Angular artery (left)
angular_artery_left.description: The angular artery is an artery of the face. It is the terminal part of the facial artery. It ascends to the medial angle of the eye's orbit. It is accompanied by the angular vein. It ends by anastomosing with the dorsal nasal branch of the ophthalmic artery.

angular_artery_right.name: Angular artery (right)
angular_artery_right.description: The angular artery is an artery of the face. It is the terminal part of the facial artery. It ascends to the medial angle of the eye's orbit. It is accompanied by the angular vein. It ends by anastomosing with the dorsal nasal branch of the ophthalmic artery.

angular_gyrus_left.name: Angular gyrus (left)
angular_gyrus_left.description: The angular gyrus is a region of the brain lying mainly in the anterolateral region of parietal lobe, that lies near the superior edge of the temporal lobe, and immediately posterior to the supramarginal gyrus.

angular_gyrus_right.name: Angular gyrus (right)
angular_gyrus_right.description: The angular gyrus is a region of the brain lying mainly in the anterolateral region of parietal lobe, that lies near the superior edge of the temporal lobe, and immediately posterior to the supramarginal gyrus.

angular_vein_left.name: Angular vein (left)
angular_vein_left.description: The angular vein is a vein of the face. It is the upper part of the facial vein, above its junction with the superior labial vein. It is formed by the junction of the supratrochlear vein and supraorbital vein, and joins with the superior labial vein. It drains the medial canthus, and parts of the nose and the upper lip.

angular_vein_right.name: Angular vein (right)
angular_vein_right.description: The angular vein is a vein of the face. It is the upper part of the facial vein, above its junction with the superior labial vein. It is formed by the junction of the supratrochlear vein and supraorbital vein, and joins with the superior labial vein. It drains the medial canthus, and parts of the nose and the upper lip.

anterior_belly_of_digastric_muscle_left.name: Anterior belly of digastric muscle (left)
anterior_belly_of_digastric_muscle_left.description: The digastric muscle (also digastricus) (named digastric as it has two 'bellies') is a small muscle located under the jaw. The term "digastric muscle" refers to this specific muscle. However, other muscles that have two separate muscle bellies include the suspensory muscle of duodenum, omohyoid, occipitofrontalis.

anterior_belly_of_digastric_muscle_right.name: Anterior belly of digastric muscle (right)
anterior_belly_of_digastric_muscle_right.description: The digastric muscle (also digastricus) (named digastric as it has two 'bellies') is a small muscle located under the jaw. The term "digastric muscle" refers to this specific muscle. However, other muscles that have two separate muscle bellies include the suspensory muscle of duodenum, omohyoid, occipitofrontalis.

anterior_cerebral_artery_left.name: Anterior cerebral artery (left)
anterior_cerebral_artery_left.description: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) is one of a pair of cerebral arteries that supplies oxygenated blood to most midline portions of the frontal lobes and superior medial parietal lobes of the brain. The two anterior cerebral arteries arise from the internal carotid artery and are part of the circle of Willis.

anterior_cerebral_artery_right.name: Anterior cerebral artery (right)
anterior_cerebral_artery_right.description: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) is one of a pair of cerebral arteries that supplies oxygenated blood to most midline portions of the frontal lobes and superior medial parietal lobes of the brain. The two anterior cerebral arteries arise from the internal carotid artery and are part of the circle of Willis.

anterior_chamber_of_eyeball_left.name: Anterior chamber of eyeball (left)
anterior_chamber_of_eyeball_left.description: The anterior chamber (AC) is the aqueous humor-filled space inside the eye between the iris and the cornea's innermost surface, the endothelium. Hyphema, anterior uveitis and glaucoma are three main pathologies in this area. In hyphema, blood fills the anterior chamber as a result of a hemorrhage, most commonly after a blunt eye injury.

anterior_chamber_of_eyeball_right.name: Anterior chamber of eyeball (right)
anterior_chamber_of_eyeball_right.description: The anterior chamber (AC) is the aqueous humor-filled space inside the eye between the iris and the cornea's innermost surface, the endothelium. Hyphema, anterior uveitis and glaucoma are three main pathologies in this area. In hyphema, blood fills the anterior chamber as a result of a hemorrhage, most commonly after a blunt eye injury.

anterior_cochlear_nucleus_left.name: Anterior cochlear nucleus (left)
anterior_cochlear_nucleus_left.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN). The ventral (anterior) cochlear nucleus is unlayered whereas the dorsal cochlear nucleus is layered.

anterior_cochlear_nucleus_right.name: Anterior cochlear nucleus (right)
anterior_cochlear_nucleus_right.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN). The ventral (anterior) cochlear nucleus is unlayered whereas the dorsal cochlear nucleus is layered.

anterior_commissure.name: Anterior commissure
anterior_commissure.description: The anterior commissure (also known as the precommissure) is a white matter tract (a bundle of axons) connecting the two temporal lobes of the cerebral hemispheres across the midline, and placed in front of the columns of the fornix.

anterior_communicating_artery.name: Anterior communicating artery
anterior_communicating_artery.description: In human anatomy, the anterior communicating artery is a blood vessel of the brain that connects the left and right anterior cerebral arteries.

anterior_division_of_mandibular_nerve_le.name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (left)
anterior_division_of_mandibular_nerve_le.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

anterior_division_of_mandibular_nerve_ri.name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (right)
anterior_division_of_mandibular_nerve_ri.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

anterior_division_of_retromandibular_vei.name: Anterior division of retromandibular vein (left)
anterior_division_of_retromandibular_vei.description: The retromandibular vein emerges from the confluence of several veins, in front of the ear, and reaches the facial vein. It is formed by the union of the superficial temporal vein and the maxillary vein.

anterior_division_of_retromandibular_vei.name: Anterior division of retromandibular vein (right)
anterior_division_of_retromandibular_vei.description: The retromandibular vein emerges from the confluence of several veins, in front of the ear, and reaches the facial vein. It is formed by the union of the superficial temporal vein and the maxillary vein.

anterior_ethmoidal_artery_left.name: Anterior ethmoidal artery (left)
anterior_ethmoidal_artery_left.description: The anterior ethmoidal artery, is a branch of the ophthalmic artery in the orbit. It exits the orbit through the anterior ethmoidal foramen. The posterior ethmoidal artery is posterior to it.

anterior_ethmoidal_artery_right.name: Anterior ethmoidal artery (right)
anterior_ethmoidal_artery_right.description: The anterior ethmoidal artery, is a branch of the ophthalmic artery in the orbit. It exits the orbit through the anterior ethmoidal foramen. The posterior ethmoidal artery is posterior to it.

anterior_inferior_cerebellar_artery_left.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery (left)
anterior_inferior_cerebellar_artery_left.description: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is one of three pairs of arteries that supplies blood to the cerebellum. It arises from the basilar artery on each side at the level of the junction between the medulla oblongata and the pons in the brainstem.

anterior_inferior_cerebellar_artery_righ.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery (right)
anterior_inferior_cerebellar_artery_righ.description: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is one of three pairs of arteries that supplies blood to the cerebellum. It arises from the basilar artery on each side at the level of the junction between the medulla oblongata and the pons in the brainstem.

anterior_intercavernous_sinus.name: Anterior intercavernous sinus
anterior_intercavernous_sinus.description: The intercavernous sinuses are two in number, an anterior and a posterior, and connect the two cavernous sinuses[1] across the middle line.

anterior_notch_of_auricle_left.name: Anterior notch of auricle (left)
anterior_notch_of_auricle_left.description: Incisure between the tragus and the crura of antihelix.

anterior_notch_of_auricle_right.name: Anterior notch of auricle (right)
anterior_notch_of_auricle_right.description: Incisure between the tragus and the crura of antihelix.

anterior_segment_of_eyeball_left.name: Anterior segment of eyeball (left)
anterior_segment_of_eyeball_left.description: The anterior segment or anterior cavity is the front third of the eye that includes the structures in front of the vitreous humour: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens. Within the anterior segment are two fluid-filled spaces: the anterior chamber between the posterior surface of the cornea (i.e. the corneal endothelium) and the iris.

anterior_segment_of_eyeball_right.name: Anterior segment of eyeball (right)
anterior_segment_of_eyeball_right.description: The anterior segment or anterior cavity is the front third of the eye that includes the structures in front of the vitreous humour: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens. Within the anterior segment are two fluid-filled spaces: the anterior chamber between the posterior surface of the cornea (i.e. the corneal endothelium) and the iris.

anterior_septal_branches_of_anterior_eth.name: Anterior septal branches of anterior ethmoidal artery (left)
Anterior septal branches of anterior ethmoidal artery (right)

anterior_spinal_artery_left.name: Anterior spinal artery (left)
anterior_spinal_artery_left.description: In human anatomy, the anterior spinal artery is the artery that supplies the anterior portion of the spinal cord. It arises from branches of the vertebral arteries and courses along the anterior aspect of the spinal cord. It is reinforced by several contributory arteries, especially the artery of Adamkiewicz.

anterior_spinal_artery_right.name: Anterior spinal artery (right)
anterior_spinal_artery_right.description: In human anatomy, the anterior spinal artery is the artery that supplies the anterior portion of the spinal cord. It arises from branches of the vertebral arteries and courses along the anterior aspect of the spinal cord. It is reinforced by several contributory arteries, especially the artery of Adamkiewicz.

antihelix_left.name: Antihelix (left)
antihelix_left.description: Arciform relief of the auricle located in front the posterior part of the helix

antihelix_right.name: Antihelix (right)
antihelix_right.description: Arciform relief of the auricle located in front the posterior part of the helix

antitragus_left.name: Antitragus (left)
antitragus_left.description: It is a small tubercle on the visible part of the ear, the pinna. The antitragus is located just above the earlobe and points anteriorly. It is separated from the tragus by the intertragic notch. The antitragicus muscle, an intrinsic muscle of the ear, arises from the outer part of the antitragus.

antitragus_right.name: Antitragus (right)
antitragus_right.description: It is a small tubercle on the visible part of the ear, the pinna. The antitragus is located just above the earlobe and points anteriorly. It is separated from the tragus by the intertragic notch. The antitragicus muscle, an intrinsic muscle of the ear, arises from the outer part of the antitragus.

articular_capsule_of_temporomandibular_j.name: Articular capsule of temporomandibular joint (left)
articular_capsule_of_temporomandibular_j.description: In anatomy, the temporomandibular joints (TMJ) are the two joints connecting the jawbone to the skull. It is a bilateral synovial articulation between the temporal bone of the skull above and the mandible below; it is from these bones that its name is derived. This joint is unique in that it is a bilateral joint that functions as one unit.

articular_capsule_of_temporomandibular_j.name: Articular capsule of temporomandibular joint (right)
articular_capsule_of_temporomandibular_j.description: In anatomy, the temporomandibular joints (TMJ) are the two joints connecting the jawbone to the skull. It is a bilateral synovial articulation between the temporal bone of the skull above and the mandible below; it is from these bones that its name is derived. This joint is unique in that it is a bilateral joint that functions as one unit.

articular_disc_of_temporomandibular_join.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint (left)
articular_disc_of_temporomandibular_join.description: The articular disk of the temporomandibular joint is a thin, oval plate made of non-vascular fibrous connective tissue, which is located between the mandible's condyloid process and the cranium's mandibular fossa.

articular_disc_of_temporomandibular_join.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint (right)
articular_disc_of_temporomandibular_join.description: The articular disk of the temporomandibular joint is a thin, oval plate made of non-vascular fibrous connective tissue, which is located between the mandible's condyloid process and the cranium's mandibular fossa.

ary_epiglottic_part_of_oblique_arytenoid.name: Ary-epiglottic part of oblique arytenoid muscle (left)
ary_epiglottic_part_of_oblique_arytenoid.description: Origin apex of arytenoid cartilage. Insertion: border of epiglottis. Support of the ary-epiglottic fold. Lower the epiglottis.

ary_epiglottic_part_of_oblique_arytenoid.name: Ary-epiglottic part of oblique arytenoid muscle (right)
ary_epiglottic_part_of_oblique_arytenoid.description: Origin apex of arytenoid cartilage. Insertion: border of epiglottis. Support of the ary-epiglottic fold. Lower the epiglottis.

ascending_part_of_trapezius_muscle_left.name: Ascending part of trapezius muscle (left)
ascending_part_of_trapezius_muscle_left.description: The trapezius is a large paired trapezoid-shaped surface muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae of the spine and laterally to the spine of the scapula. It moves the scapula and supports the arm.

ascending_part_of_trapezius_muscle_right.name: Ascending part of trapezius muscle (right)
ascending_part_of_trapezius_muscle_right.description: The trapezius is a large paired trapezoid-shaped surface muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae of the spine and laterally to the spine of the scapula. It moves the scapula and supports the arm.

ascending_pharyngeal_artery_left.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery (left)
ascending_pharyngeal_artery_left.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is an artery in the neck that supplies the pharynx, developing from the proximal part of the embryonic second aortic arch.

ascending_pharyngeal_artery_right.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery (right)
ascending_pharyngeal_artery_right.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is an artery in the neck that supplies the pharynx, developing from the proximal part of the embryonic second aortic arch.

atlas_c1.name: Atlas (C1)
atlas_c1.description: In anatomy, the atlas (C1) is the most superior (first) cervical vertebra of the spine and is located in the neck. It is named for Atlas of Greek mythology because, just as Atlas supported the globe, it supports the entire head.

auditory_tube_left.name: Auditory tube (left)
auditory_tube_left.description: In anatomy, the Eustachian tube, also known as the auditory tube or pharyngotympanic tube, is a tube that links the nasopharynx to the middle ear, of which it is also a part. In adult humans, the Eustachian tube is approximately 35 mm (1.4 in) long and 3 mm (0.12 in) in diameter.

auditory_tube_right.name: Auditory tube (right)
auditory_tube_right.description: In anatomy, the Eustachian tube, also known as the auditory tube or pharyngotympanic tube, is a tube that links the nasopharynx to the middle ear, of which it is also a part. In adult humans, the Eustachian tube is approximately 35 mm (1.4 in) long and 3 mm (0.12 in) in diameter.

auricular_region_left.name: Auricular region (left)
auricular_region_left.description: The ears are referred to as the auricular region, or otic region. See: ear, external ear

auricular_region_right.name: Auricular region (right)
auricular_region_right.description: The ears are referred to as the auricular region, or otic region. See: ear, external ear

axis_c2.name: Axis (C2)
axis_c2.description: In anatomy, the axis (from Latin axis, "axle") or epistropheus, is the second cervical vertebra (C2) of the spine, immediately posterior to the atlas, upon which the head rests. The axis' defining feature is its strong odontoid process (bony protrusion) known as the dens, which rises dorsally from the rest of the bone.

basilar_artery.name: Basilar artery
basilar_artery.description: The basilar artery () is one of the arteries that supplies the brain with oxygen-rich blood.

basilar_venous_plexus.name: Basilar venous plexus
basilar_venous_plexus.description: The basilar plexus (transverse or basilar sinus) consists of several interlacing venous channels between the layers of the dura mater over the basilar part of the occipital bone (the clivus), and serves to connect the two inferior petrosal sinuses. It communicates with the anterior vertebral venous plexus.

buccal_artery_left.name: Buccal artery (left)
buccal_artery_left.description: The buccal artery (buccinator artery) is a small artery in the head. It branches off the second part of the maxillary artery and supplies the cheek and buccinator muscle.

buccal_artery_right.name: Buccal artery (right)
buccal_artery_right.description: The buccal artery (buccinator artery) is a small artery in the head. It branches off the second part of the maxillary artery and supplies the cheek and buccinator muscle.

buccal_nerve_left.name: Buccal nerve (left)
buccal_nerve_left.description: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face. It is a branch of the mandibular nerve (which is itself a branch of the trigeminal nerve) and transmits sensory information from skin over the buccal membrane (in general, the cheek) and from the second and third molar teeth.

buccal_nerve_right.name: Buccal nerve (right)
buccal_nerve_right.description: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face. It is a branch of the mandibular nerve (which is itself a branch of the trigeminal nerve) and transmits sensory information from skin over the buccal membrane (in general, the cheek) and from the second and third molar teeth.

buccal_region_left.name: Buccal region (left)
buccal_region_left.description: The cheeks are referred to as the buccal region.

buccal_region_right.name: Buccal region (right)
buccal_region_right.description: The cheeks are referred to as the buccal region.

bucinator_left.name: Bucinator (left)
bucinator_left.description: The bucinator is a thin quadrilateral muscle occupying the interval between the maxilla and the mandible at the side of the face. It forms the anterior part of the cheek or the lateral wall of the oral cavity.

bucinator_node_left.name: Bucinator node (left)
bucinator_node_left.description: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buccinator_lymph_node

bucinator_node_right.name: Bucinator node (right)
bucinator_node_right.description: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buccinator_lymph_node

bucinator_right.name: Bucinator (right)
bucinator_right.description: The bucinator is a thin quadrilateral muscle occupying the interval between the maxilla and the mandible at the side of the face. It forms the anterior part of the cheek or the lateral wall of the oral cavity.

calcarine_sulcus_left.name: Calcarine sulcus (left)
calcarine_sulcus_left.description: The calcarine sulcus (or calcarine fissure) is an anatomical landmark located at the caudal end of the medial surface of the brain of humans and other primates. Its name comes from the Latin "calcar" meaning "spur". It is very deep and known as a complete sulcus.

calcarine_sulcus_right.name: Calcarine sulcus (right)
calcarine_sulcus_right.description: The calcarine sulcus (or calcarine fissure) is an anatomical landmark located at the caudal end of the medial surface of the brain of humans and other primates. Its name comes from the Latin "calcar" meaning "spur". It is very deep and known as a complete sulcus.

callosomarginal_artery_left.name: Callosomarginal artery (left)
callosomarginal_artery_left.description: A2 extends from the AComm to the bifurcation forming the pericallosal and callosomarginal arteries. The recurrent artery of Heubner (distal medial striate artery), which irrigates the internal capsule, usually arises at the beginning of this segment near the AComm.

callosomarginal_artery_right.name: Callosomarginal artery (right)
callosomarginal_artery_right.description: A2 extends from the AComm to the bifurcation forming the pericallosal and callosomarginal arteries. The recurrent artery of Heubner (distal medial striate artery), which irrigates the internal capsule, usually arises at the beginning of this segment near the AComm.

carotid_triangle_left.name: Carotid triangle (left)
carotid_triangle_left.description: The carotid triangle (or superior carotid triangle) is a portion of the anterior triangle of the neck.

carotid_triangle_right.name: Carotid triangle (right)
carotid_triangle_right.description: The carotid triangle (or superior carotid triangle) is a portion of the anterior triangle of the neck.

caudate_nucleus_left.name: Caudate nucleus (left)
caudate_nucleus_left.description: The caudate nucleus is one of the structures that make up the corpus striatum, which is a component of the basal ganglia.

caudate_nucleus_right.name: Caudate nucleus (right)
caudate_nucleus_right.description: The caudate nucleus is one of the structures that make up the corpus striatum, which is a component of the basal ganglia.

cavernous_sinus_left.name: Cavernous sinus (left)
cavernous_sinus_left.description: The cavernous sinus within the human head is one of the dural venous sinuses creating a cavity called the lateral sellar compartment bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.

cavernous_sinus_right.name: Cavernous sinus (right)
cavernous_sinus_right.description: The cavernous sinus within the human head is one of the dural venous sinuses creating a cavity called the lateral sellar compartment bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.

cavity_of_concha_left.name: Cavity of concha (left)
cavity_of_concha_left.description: Concha is the hollow next to the ear canal.

cavity_of_concha_right.name: Cavity of concha (right)
cavity_of_concha_right.description: Concha is the hollow next to the ear canal.

central_lobule.name: Central lobule
central_lobule.description: The central lobule is a small square lobule, situated in the anterior cerebellar notch.

central_retinal_artery_left.name: Central retinal artery (left)
central_retinal_artery_left.description: The central retinal artery (retinal artery) branches off the ophthalmic artery, running inferior to the optic nerve within its dural sheath to the eyeball.

central_retinal_artery_right.name: Central retinal artery (right)
central_retinal_artery_right.description: The central retinal artery (retinal artery) branches off the ophthalmic artery, running inferior to the optic nerve within its dural sheath to the eyeball.

central_sulcus_left.name: Central sulcus (left)
central_sulcus_left.description: The central sulcus is a sulcus, or groove, in the cerebral cortex in the brains of vertebrates. Also called the central fissure, or the fissure of Rolando or the Rolandic fissure, after Luigi Rolando. It is sometimes confused with the longitudinal fissure.

central_sulcus_right.name: Central sulcus (right)
central_sulcus_right.description: The central sulcus is a sulcus, or groove, in the cerebral cortex in the brains of vertebrates. Also called the central fissure, or the fissure of Rolando or the Rolandic fissure, after Luigi Rolando. It is sometimes confused with the longitudinal fissure.

chorda_tympani_left.name: Chorda tympani (left)
chorda_tympani_left.description: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

chorda_tympani_right.name: Chorda tympani (right)
chorda_tympani_right.description: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

choroid_plexus_left.name: Choroid plexus (left)
choroid_plexus_left.description: The choroid plexus, or plica choroidea, is a plexus of cells that arises from the tela choroidea in each of the ventricles of the brain. The choroid plexus produces most of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of the central nervous system. CSF is produced and secreted by the regions of the choroid plexus.

choroid_plexus_right.name: Choroid plexus (right)
choroid_plexus_right.description: The choroid plexus, or plica choroidea, is a plexus of cells that arises from the tela choroidea in each of the ventricles of the brain. The choroid plexus produces most of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of the central nervous system. CSF is produced and secreted by the regions of the choroid plexus.

cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_anteri.name: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part) (left)
cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_anteri.description: The cingulate cortex is a part of the brain situated in the medial aspect of the cerebral cortex. The cingulate cortex includes the entire cingulate gyrus, which lies immediately above the corpus callosum, and the continuation of this in the cingulate sulcus. The cingulate cortex is usually considered part of the limbic lobe.

cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_anteri.name: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part) (right)
cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_anteri.description: The cingulate cortex is a part of the brain situated in the medial aspect of the cerebral cortex. The cingulate cortex includes the entire cingulate gyrus, which lies immediately above the corpus callosum, and the continuation of this in the cingulate sulcus. The cingulate cortex is usually considered part of the limbic lobe.

cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_poster.name: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part) (left)
cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_poster.description: The cingulate sulcus is a sulcus (brain fold) on the cingulate cortex in the medial wall of the cerebral cortex. The frontal and parietal lobes are separated from the cingulate gyrus by the cingulate sulcus. It terminates as the marginal sulcus of the cingulate sulcus.

cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_poster.name: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle posterior part) (right)
cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_middle_poster.description: The cingulate sulcus is a sulcus (brain fold) on the cingulate cortex in the medial wall of the cerebral cortex. The frontal and parietal lobes are separated from the cingulate gyrus by the cingulate sulcus. It terminates as the marginal sulcus of the cingulate sulcus.

cingulate_gyrus_and_sulcus_posterior_dor.name: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part) (left)
Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posterior dorsal part) (right)

cingulate_gyrus_posteroventral_part_left.name: Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral part*) (left)
cingulate_gyrus_posteroventral_part_left.description: The cingulate cortex is a part of the brain situated in the medial aspect of the cerebral cortex. The cingulate cortex includes the entire cingulate gyrus, which lies immediately above the corpus callosum, and the continuation of this in the cingulate sulcus. The cingulate cortex is usually considered part of the limbic lobe.

cingulate_gyrus_posteroventral_part_righ.name: Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral part*) (right)
cingulate_gyrus_posteroventral_part_righ.description: The cingulate cortex is a part of the brain situated in the medial aspect of the cerebral cortex. The cingulate cortex includes the entire cingulate gyrus, which lies immediately above the corpus callosum, and the continuation of this in the cingulate sulcus. The cingulate cortex is usually considered part of the limbic lobe.

cingulate_sulcus_marginal_part_left.name: Cingulate sulcus (Marginal part*) (left)
cingulate_sulcus_marginal_part_left.description: The cingulate sulcus is a sulcus (brain fold) on the cingulate cortex in the medial wall of the cerebral cortex. The frontal and parietal lobes are separated from the cingulate gyrus by the cingulate sulcus. It terminates as the marginal sulcus of the cingulate sulcus.

cingulate_sulcus_marginal_part_right.name: Cingulate sulcus (Marginal part*) (right)
cingulate_sulcus_marginal_part_right.description: The cingulate sulcus is a sulcus (brain fold) on the cingulate cortex in the medial wall of the cerebral cortex. The frontal and parietal lobes are separated from the cingulate gyrus by the cingulate sulcus. It terminates as the marginal sulcus of the cingulate sulcus.

circular_sulcus_of_insula_left.name: Circular sulcus of insula (left)
circular_sulcus_of_insula_left.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

circular_sulcus_of_insula_right.name: Circular sulcus of insula (right)
circular_sulcus_of_insula_right.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

collateral_sulcus_left.name: Collateral sulcus (left)
collateral_sulcus_left.description: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

collateral_sulcus_right.name: Collateral sulcus (right)
collateral_sulcus_right.description: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

common_facial_vein_left.name: Common facial vein (left)
common_facial_vein_left.description: The facial vein usually unites with the anterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which crosses the external carotid artery and enters the internal jugular vein at a variable point below the hyoid bone.

common_facial_vein_right.name: Common facial vein (right)
common_facial_vein_right.description: The facial vein usually unites with the anterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which crosses the external carotid artery and enters the internal jugular vein at a variable point below the hyoid bone.

common_tendinous_ring_left.name: Common tendinous ring (left)
common_tendinous_ring_left.description: The common tendinous ring, also known as the annulus of Zinn, or annular tendon, is a ring of fibrous tissue surrounding the optic nerve at its entrance at the apex of the orbit. It is the common origin of the four recti muscles of the group of extraocular muscles. It can be used to divide the regions of the superior orbital fissure.

common_tendinous_ring_right.name: Common tendinous ring (right)
common_tendinous_ring_right.description: The common tendinous ring, also known as the annulus of Zinn, or annular tendon, is a ring of fibrous tissue surrounding the optic nerve at its entrance at the apex of the orbit. It is the common origin of the four recti muscles of the group of extraocular muscles. It can be used to divide the regions of the superior orbital fissure.

concha_of_auricle_left.name: Concha of auricle (left)
concha_of_auricle_left.description: Concha is the hollow next to the ear canal.

concha_of_auricle_right.name: Concha of auricle (right)
concha_of_auricle_right.description: Concha is the hollow next to the ear canal.

cornea_left.name: Cornea (left)
cornea_left.description: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber. Along with the anterior chamber and lens, the cornea refracts light, accounting for approximately two-thirds of the eye's total optical power. In humans, the refractive power of the cornea is approximately 43 dioptres.

cornea_right.name: Cornea (right)
cornea_right.description: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber. Along with the anterior chamber and lens, the cornea refracts light, accounting for approximately two-thirds of the eye's total optical power. In humans, the refractive power of the cornea is approximately 43 dioptres.

corniculate_cartilage_left.name: Corniculate cartilage (left)
corniculate_cartilage_left.description: The corniculate cartilages are two small conical nodules consisting of elastic cartilage, which articulate with the summits of the arytenoid cartilages and serve to prolong them posteriorly and medially.

corniculate_cartilage_right.name: Corniculate cartilage (right)
corniculate_cartilage_right.description: The corniculate cartilages are two small conical nodules consisting of elastic cartilage, which articulate with the summits of the arytenoid cartilages and serve to prolong them posteriorly and medially.

corpus_callosum.name: Corpus callosum
corpus_callosum.description: The corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain. The corpus callosum is only found in placental mammals.

corrugator_supercilii_left.name: Corrugator supercilii (left)
corrugator_supercilii_left.description: The corrugator supercilii muscle is a small, narrow, pyramidal muscle close to the eye. It arises from the medial end of the superciliary arch, and inserts into the deep surface of the skin of the eyebrow. It draws the eyebrow downward and medially, producing the vertical wrinkles of the forehead.

corrugator_supercilii_right.name: Corrugator supercilii (right)
corrugator_supercilii_right.description: The corrugator supercilii muscle is a small, narrow, pyramidal muscle close to the eye. It arises from the medial end of the superciliary arch, and inserts into the deep surface of the skin of the eyebrow. It draws the eyebrow downward and medially, producing the vertical wrinkles of the forehead.

crura_of_antihelix_left.name: Crura of antihelix (left)
crura_of_antihelix_left.description: Each of the two upper divisions of the antihelix, surrounding the triangular fossa.

crura_of_antihelix_right.name: Crura of antihelix (right)
crura_of_antihelix_right.description: Each of the two upper divisions of the antihelix, surrounding the triangular fossa.

culmen.name: Culmen
culmen.description: A culmen is a top, a summit or a culminating point. It may also refer to: Culmen (bird), the upper ridge of a bird's beak Culmen (cerebellum), a structure in the brain https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culmen

cuneate_fasciculus.name: Cuneate fasciculus
cuneate_fasciculus.description: The cuneate fasciculus is triangular on transverse section, and lies between the gracile fasciculus and the posterior column, its base corresponding with the surface of the spinal cord. Its fibers, larger than those of the gracile fasciculus, are mostly derived from the same source, viz., the posterior nerve roots.

cuneus_left.name: Cuneus (left)
cuneus_left.description: The cuneus (Latin for "wedge"; plural, cunei) is a smaller lobe in the occipital lobe of the brain. The cuneus is bounded anteriorly by the parieto-occipital sulcus, inferiorly by the calcarine sulcus.

cuneus_right.name: Cuneus (right)
cuneus_right.description: The cuneus (Latin for "wedge"; plural, cunei) is a smaller lobe in the occipital lobe of the brain. The cuneus is bounded anteriorly by the parieto-occipital sulcus, inferiorly by the calcarine sulcus.

cymba_conchae_left.name: Cymba conchae (left)
cymba_conchae_left.description: Cymba conchae is the narrowest end of the concha.

cymba_conchae_right.name: Cymba conchae (right)
cymba_conchae_right.description: Cymba conchae is the narrowest end of the concha.

deep_part_of_masseter_left.name: Deep part of masseter (left)
deep_part_of_masseter_left.description: In human anatomy, the masseter is one of the muscles of mastication. Found only in mammals, it is particularly powerful in herbivores to facilitate chewing of plant matter. The most obvious muscle of mastication is the masseter muscle, since it is the most superficial and one of the strongest.

deep_part_of_masseter_right.name: Deep part of masseter (right)
deep_part_of_masseter_right.description: In human anatomy, the masseter is one of the muscles of mastication. Found only in mammals, it is particularly powerful in herbivores to facilitate chewing of plant matter. The most obvious muscle of mastication is the masseter muscle, since it is the most superficial and one of the strongest.

depressor_anguli_oris_left.name: Depressor anguli oris (left)
depressor_anguli_oris_left.description: The depressor anguli oris muscle (triangularis muscle) is a facial muscle. It originates from the mandible and inserts into the angle of the mouth. It is associated with frowning, as it depresses the corner of the mouth.

depressor_anguli_oris_right.name: Depressor anguli oris (right)
depressor_anguli_oris_right.description: The depressor anguli oris muscle (triangularis muscle) is a facial muscle. It originates from the mandible and inserts into the angle of the mouth. It is associated with frowning, as it depresses the corner of the mouth.

depressor_labii_inferioris_left.name: Depressor labii inferioris (left)
depressor_labii_inferioris_left.description: The depressor labii inferioris (or quadratus labii inferioris) is a facial muscle. It helps to lower the bottom lip.

depressor_labii_inferioris_right.name: Depressor labii inferioris (right)
depressor_labii_inferioris_right.description: The depressor labii inferioris (or quadratus labii inferioris) is a facial muscle. It helps to lower the bottom lip.

depressor_septi_nasi_left.name: Depressor septi nasi (left)
depressor_septi_nasi_left.description: The depressor septi nasi muscle (or depressor alae nasi muscle) is a muscle of the face. It connects the incisive fossa of the maxilla and the orbicularis oris muscle to the nasal septum of the nose. It draws the ala of the nose downwards, reducing the size of the nostrils.

depressor_septi_nasi_right.name: Depressor septi nasi (right)
depressor_septi_nasi_right.description: The depressor septi nasi muscle (or depressor alae nasi muscle) is a muscle of the face. It connects the incisive fossa of the maxilla and the orbicularis oris muscle to the nasal septum of the nose. It draws the ala of the nose downwards, reducing the size of the nostrils.

descending_palatine_artery_left.name: Descending palatine artery (left)
descending_palatine_artery_left.description: The descending palatine artery is a branch of the third part of the maxillary artery supplying the hard and soft palate.

descending_palatine_artery_right.name: Descending palatine artery (right)
descending_palatine_artery_right.description: The descending palatine artery is a branch of the third part of the maxillary artery supplying the hard and soft palate.

epicranial_aponeurosis_left.name: Epicranial aponeurosis (left)
epicranial_aponeurosis_left.description: The epicranial aponeurosis (aponeurosis epicranialis, galea aponeurotica) is an aponeurosis (a tough layer of dense fibrous tissue). It covers the upper part of the skull in humans and many other animals.

epicranial_aponeurosis_right.name: Epicranial aponeurosis (right)
epicranial_aponeurosis_right.description: The epicranial aponeurosis (aponeurosis epicranialis, galea aponeurotica) is an aponeurosis (a tough layer of dense fibrous tissue). It covers the upper part of the skull in humans and many other animals.

epiglottis.name: Epiglottis
epiglottis.description: The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped flap in the throat that prevents food from entering the windpipe and the lungs. It stays open during breathing, allowing air into the larynx. During swallowing, it closes to prevent aspiration of food into the lungs, forcing the swallowed liquids or food to go along the esophagus toward the stomach instead.

ethmoid_bone.name: Ethmoid bone
ethmoid_bone.description: The ethmoid bone (from Greek ethmos, "sieve") is an unpaired bone in the skull that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. It is located at the roof of the nose, between the two orbits. The cubical bone is lightweight due to a spongy construction. The ethmoid bone is one of the bones that make up the orbit of the eye.

external_carotid_artery_left.name: External carotid artery (left)
external_carotid_artery_left.description: The external carotid artery is a major artery of the head and neck. It arises from the common carotid artery when it splits into the external and internal carotid artery. External carotid artery supplies blood to the face and neck.

external_carotid_artery_right.name: External carotid artery (right)
external_carotid_artery_right.description: The external carotid artery is a major artery of the head and neck. It arises from the common carotid artery when it splits into the external and internal carotid artery. External carotid artery supplies blood to the face and neck.

eyebrow_left.name: Eyebrow (left)
eyebrow_left.description: An eyebrow is an area of short hairs above each eye that follows the shape of the lower margin of the brow ridges of some mammals. In humans, eyebrows serve two main functions: first, communication through facial expression, and second, prevention of sweat, water, and other debris from falling down into the eye socket.

eyebrow_right.name: Eyebrow (right)
eyebrow_right.description: An eyebrow is an area of short hairs above each eye that follows the shape of the lower margin of the brow ridges of some mammals. In humans, eyebrows serve two main functions: first, communication through facial expression, and second, prevention of sweat, water, and other debris from falling down into the eye socket.

facial_artery_left.name: Facial artery (left)
facial_artery_left.description: The facial artery (external maxillary artery in older texts) is a branch of the external carotid artery that supplies structures of the superficial face.

facial_artery_right.name: Facial artery (right)
facial_artery_right.description: The facial artery (external maxillary artery in older texts) is a branch of the external carotid artery that supplies structures of the superficial face.

facial_nerve_vii_left.name: Facial nerve (VII) (left)
facial_nerve_vii_left.description: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII. It emerges from the pons of the brainstem, controls the muscles of facial expression, and functions in the conveyance of taste sensations from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

facial_nerve_vii_right.name: Facial nerve (VII) (right)
facial_nerve_vii_right.description: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII. It emerges from the pons of the brainstem, controls the muscles of facial expression, and functions in the conveyance of taste sensations from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

facial_vein_left.name: Facial vein (left)
facial_vein_left.description: The facial vein (or anterior facial vein) is a relatively large vein in the human face. It commences at the side of the root of the nose and is a direct continuation of the angular vein where it also receives a small nasal branch. It lies behind the facial artery and follows a less tortuous course.

facial_vein_right.name: Facial vein (right)
facial_vein_right.description: The facial vein (or anterior facial vein) is a relatively large vein in the human face. It commences at the side of the root of the nose and is a direct continuation of the angular vein where it also receives a small nasal branch. It lies behind the facial artery and follows a less tortuous course.

falx_cerebri.name: Falx cerebri
falx_cerebri.description: The falx cerebri, also known as the cerebral falx, is a large, crescent-shaped fold of meningeal layer of dura mater that descends vertically in the longitudinal fissure between the cerebral hemispheres of the human brain.

flocculus_left.name: Flocculus (left)
flocculus_left.description: The flocculus (Latin: tuft of wool, diminutive) is a small lobe of the cerebellum at the posterior border of the middle cerebellar peduncle anterior to the biventer lobule. Like other parts of the cerebellum, the flocculus is involved in motor control.

flocculus_right.name: Flocculus (right)
flocculus_right.description: The flocculus (Latin: tuft of wool, diminutive) is a small lobe of the cerebellum at the posterior border of the middle cerebellar peduncle anterior to the biventer lobule. Like other parts of the cerebellum, the flocculus is involved in motor control.

fornix_left.name: Fornix (left)
fornix_left.description: The fornix (meaning "arch" in Latin) is a C-shaped bundle of nerve fibers in the brain that acts as the major output tract of the hippocampus. The fornix also carries some afferent fibers to the hippocampus from structures in the diencephalon and basal forebrain. The fornix is part of the limbic system.

fornix_right.name: Fornix (right)
fornix_right.description: The fornix (meaning "arch" in Latin) is a C-shaped bundle of nerve fibers in the brain that acts as the major output tract of the hippocampus. The fornix also carries some afferent fibers to the hippocampus from structures in the diencephalon and basal forebrain. The fornix is part of the limbic system.

fossa_antihelica_left.name: Fossa antihelica (left)
fossa_antihelica_left.description: Depression at the posterior surface of the auricular cartilage, corresponding to the root of the helix on the anterior surface.

fossa_antihelica_right.name: Fossa antihelica (right)
fossa_antihelica_right.description: Depression at the posterior surface of the auricular cartilage, corresponding to the root of the helix on the anterior surface.

fourth_ventricle.name: Fourth ventricle
fourth_ventricle.description: The fourth ventricle is one of the four connected fluid-filled cavities within the human brain. These cavities, known collectively as the ventricular system, consist of the left and right lateral ventricles, the third ventricle, and the fourth ventricle.

frontal_bone.name: Frontal bone
frontal_bone.description: The frontal bone is a bone in the human skull. The bone consists of two portions. These are the vertically oriented squamous part, and the horizontally oriented orbital part, making up the bony part of the forehead, part of the bony orbital cavity holding the eye, and part of the bony part of the nose respectively.

frontal_branch_of_superficial_temporal_a.name: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery (left)
Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery (right)

frontalis_muscle_left.name: Frontalis muscle (left)
frontalis_muscle_left.description: The frontalis muscle (from Latin 'frontal muscle') is a muscle which covers parts of the forehead of the skull. Some sources consider the frontalis muscle to be a distinct muscle. However, Terminologia Anatomica currently classifies it as part of the occipitofrontalis muscle along with the occipitalis muscle.

frontalis_muscle_right.name: Frontalis muscle (right)
frontalis_muscle_right.description: The frontalis muscle (from Latin 'frontal muscle') is a muscle which covers parts of the forehead of the skull. Some sources consider the frontalis muscle to be a distinct muscle. However, Terminologia Anatomica currently classifies it as part of the occipitofrontalis muscle along with the occipitalis muscle.

genioglossus_muscle_left.name: Genioglossus muscle (left)
genioglossus_muscle_left.description: The genioglossus is one of the paired extrinsic muscles of the tongue. The genioglossus is the major muscle responsible for protruding (or sticking out) the tongue.

genioglossus_muscle_right.name: Genioglossus muscle (right)
genioglossus_muscle_right.description: The genioglossus is one of the paired extrinsic muscles of the tongue. The genioglossus is the major muscle responsible for protruding (or sticking out) the tongue.

geniohyoid_muscle_left.name: Geniohyoid muscle (left)
geniohyoid_muscle_left.description: The geniohyoid muscle is a narrow muscle situated superior to the medial border of the mylohyoid muscle. It is named for its passage from the chin ("genio-" is a standard prefix for "chin") to the hyoid bone.

geniohyoid_muscle_right.name: Geniohyoid muscle (right)
geniohyoid_muscle_right.description: The geniohyoid muscle is a narrow muscle situated superior to the medial border of the mylohyoid muscle. It is named for its passage from the chin ("genio-" is a standard prefix for "chin") to the hyoid bone.

gingiva.name: Gingiva
gingiva.description: The gums or gingiva (plural: gingivae) consist of the mucosal tissue that lies over the mandible and maxilla inside the mouth. Gum health and disease can have an effect on general health.

glossopharyngeal_nerve_ix_left.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (left)
glossopharyngeal_nerve_ix_left.description: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information. It exits the brainstem out from the sides of the upper medulla, just anterior (closer to the nose) to the vagus nerve.

glossopharyngeal_nerve_ix_right.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (right)
glossopharyngeal_nerve_ix_right.description: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information. It exits the brainstem out from the sides of the upper medulla, just anterior (closer to the nose) to the vagus nerve.

greater_palatine_artery_left.name: Greater palatine artery (left)
greater_palatine_artery_left.description: The greater palatine artery is a branch of the descending palatine artery (a terminal branch of the maxillary artery) and contributes to the blood supply of the hard palate and nasal septum.

greater_palatine_artery_right.name: Greater palatine artery (right)
greater_palatine_artery_right.description: The greater palatine artery is a branch of the descending palatine artery (a terminal branch of the maxillary artery) and contributes to the blood supply of the hard palate and nasal septum.

habenula.name: Habenula
habenula.description: In neuroanatomy, habenula (diminutive of Latin habena meaning rein) originally denoted the stalk of the pineal gland (pineal habenula; pedunculus of pineal body), but gradually came to refer to a neighboring group of nerve cells with which the pineal gland was believed to be associated, the habenular nucleus.

helix_left.name: Helix (left)
helix_left.description: External curvy border of the auricle

helix_right.name: Helix (right)
helix_right.description: External curvy border of the auricle

hippocampal_commissure.name: Hippocampal commissure
hippocampal_commissure.description: The lateral portions of the body of the fornix are joined by a thin triangular lamina, named the psalterium (lyra). This lamina contains some commissural fibers that connect the two hippocampi across the middle line and constitute the commissure of fornix (also called the hippocampal commissure).

hippocampus_left.name: Hippocampus (left)
hippocampus_left.description: The hippocampus (via Latin from Greek ἱππόκαμπος, 'seahorse') is a major component of the brain of humans and other vertebrates. Humans and other mammals have two hippocampi, one in each side of the brain.

hippocampus_right.name: Hippocampus (right)
hippocampus_right.description: The hippocampus (via Latin from Greek ἱππόκαμπος, 'seahorse') is a major component of the brain of humans and other vertebrates. Humans and other mammals have two hippocampi, one in each side of the brain.

hyoglossus_muscle_left.name: Hyoglossus muscle (left)
hyoglossus_muscle_left.description: The hyoglossus, thin and quadrilateral, arises from the side of the body and from the whole length of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone, and passes almost vertically upward to enter the side of the tongue, between the styloglossus and the inferior longitudinal muscle of the tongue. It forms a part of the floor of submandibular triangle.

hyoglossus_muscle_right.name: Hyoglossus muscle (right)
hyoglossus_muscle_right.description: The hyoglossus, thin and quadrilateral, arises from the side of the body and from the whole length of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone, and passes almost vertically upward to enter the side of the tongue, between the styloglossus and the inferior longitudinal muscle of the tongue. It forms a part of the floor of submandibular triangle.

hyoid_bone.name: Hyoid bone
hyoid_bone.description: The hyoid bone (lingual bone or tongue-bone) () is a horseshoe-shaped bone situated in the anterior midline of the neck between the chin and the thyroid cartilage. At rest, it lies at the level of the base of the mandible in the front and the third cervical vertebra (C3) behind.

hypoglossal_nerve_xii_left.name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (left)
hypoglossal_nerve_xii_left.description: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve. It is a nerve with a solely motor function.

hypoglossal_nerve_xii_right.name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (right)
hypoglossal_nerve_xii_right.description: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve. It is a nerve with a solely motor function.

inferior_alveolar_artery_left.name: Inferior alveolar artery (left)
inferior_alveolar_artery_left.description: The inferior alveolar artery (inferior dental artery) is an artery of the face. It is a branch of the first portion of the maxillary artery.

inferior_alveolar_artery_right.name: Inferior alveolar artery (right)
inferior_alveolar_artery_right.description: The inferior alveolar artery (inferior dental artery) is an artery of the face. It is a branch of the first portion of the maxillary artery.

inferior_alveolar_nerve_left.name: Inferior alveolar nerve (left)
inferior_alveolar_nerve_left.description: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve. The inferior alveolar nerves supply sensation to the lower teeth.

inferior_alveolar_nerve_right.name: Inferior alveolar nerve (right)
inferior_alveolar_nerve_right.description: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve. The inferior alveolar nerves supply sensation to the lower teeth.

inferior_colliculus_left.name: Inferior colliculus (left)
inferior_colliculus_left.description: The inferior colliculus (IC) (Latin for lower hill) is the principal midbrain nucleus of the auditory pathway and receives input from several peripheral brainstem nuclei in the auditory pathway, as well as inputs from the auditory cortex.

inferior_colliculus_right.name: Inferior colliculus (right)
inferior_colliculus_right.description: The inferior colliculus (IC) (Latin for lower hill) is the principal midbrain nucleus of the auditory pathway and receives input from several peripheral brainstem nuclei in the auditory pathway, as well as inputs from the auditory cortex.

inferior_frontal_sulcus_left.name: Inferior frontal sulcus (left)
inferior_frontal_sulcus_left.description: The inferior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the middle frontal gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_frontal_sulcus

inferior_frontal_sulcus_right.name: Inferior frontal sulcus (right)
inferior_frontal_sulcus_right.description: The inferior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the middle frontal gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_frontal_sulcus

inferior_head_of_lateral_pterygoid_muscl.name: Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscle (left)
inferior_head_of_lateral_pterygoid_muscl.description: The lateral pterygoid or external pterygoid is a muscle of mastication with two heads. It lies superiorly to the medial pterygoid.

inferior_head_of_lateral_pterygoid_muscl.name: Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscle (right)
inferior_head_of_lateral_pterygoid_muscl.description: The lateral pterygoid or external pterygoid is a muscle of mastication with two heads. It lies superiorly to the medial pterygoid.

inferior_labial_artery_left.name: Inferior labial artery (left)
inferior_labial_artery_left.description: The inferior labial artery (inferior labial branch of facial artery) arises near the angle of the mouth as a branch of the facial artery; it passes upward and forward beneath the triangularis and, penetrating the orbicularis oris, runs in a tortuous course along the edge of the lower lip between this muscle and the mucous membrane.

inferior_labial_artery_right.name: Inferior labial artery (right)
inferior_labial_artery_right.description: The inferior labial artery (inferior labial branch of facial artery) arises near the angle of the mouth as a branch of the facial artery; it passes upward and forward beneath the triangularis and, penetrating the orbicularis oris, runs in a tortuous course along the edge of the lower lip between this muscle and the mucous membrane.

inferior_labial_veins_left.name: Inferior labial veins (left)
inferior_labial_veins_left.description: The inferior labial veins drain the blood of the inferior part of the oral region to the facial vein, then to the common facial vein, then to the internal jugular vein.

inferior_labial_veins_right.name: Inferior labial veins (right)
inferior_labial_veins_right.description: The inferior labial veins drain the blood of the inferior part of the oral region to the facial vein, then to the common facial vein, then to the internal jugular vein.

inferior_nasal_concha_bone_left.name: Inferior nasal concha bone (left)
inferior_nasal_concha_bone_left.description: The inferior nasal concha (inferior turbinated bone or inferior turbinal/turbinate) is one of the three paired nasal conchae in the nose. It extends horizontally along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity and consists of a lamina of spongy bone, curled upon itself like a scroll, (turbinate meaning inverted cone).

inferior_nasal_concha_bone_right.name: Inferior nasal concha bone (right)
inferior_nasal_concha_bone_right.description: The inferior nasal concha (inferior turbinated bone or inferior turbinal/turbinate) is one of the three paired nasal conchae in the nose. It extends horizontally along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity and consists of a lamina of spongy bone, curled upon itself like a scroll, (turbinate meaning inverted cone).

inferior_oblique_muscle_left.name: Inferior oblique muscle (left)
inferior_oblique_muscle_left.description: The inferior oblique muscle or obliquus oculi inferior is a thin, narrow muscle placed near the anterior margin of the floor of the orbit. The inferior oblique is one of the extraocular muscles, and is attached to the maxillary bone (origin) and the posterior, inferior, lateral surface of the eye (insertion).

inferior_oblique_muscle_right.name: Inferior oblique muscle (right)
inferior_oblique_muscle_right.description: The inferior oblique muscle or obliquus oculi inferior is a thin, narrow muscle placed near the anterior margin of the floor of the orbit. The inferior oblique is one of the extraocular muscles, and is attached to the maxillary bone (origin) and the posterior, inferior, lateral surface of the eye (insertion).

inferior_occipital_gyrus_and_sulcus_left.name: Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus* (left)
inferior_occipital_gyrus_and_sulcus_left.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain. The gyri are the superior occipital gyrus, the middle occipital gyrus, and the inferior occipital gyrus, and these are also known as the occipital face area.

inferior_occipital_gyrus_and_sulcus_righ.name: Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus* (right)
inferior_occipital_gyrus_and_sulcus_righ.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain. The gyri are the superior occipital gyrus, the middle occipital gyrus, and the inferior occipital gyrus, and these are also known as the occipital face area.

inferior_ophthalmic_vein_left.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein (left)
inferior_ophthalmic_vein_left.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein is a vein of the orbit around the eye. It receives veins from many structures. It divides into two branches, one of which ends in the pterygoid plexus through the inferior orbital fissure, and the other which ends in the cavernous sinus through the superior orbital fissure.

inferior_ophthalmic_vein_right.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein (right)
inferior_ophthalmic_vein_right.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein is a vein of the orbit around the eye. It receives veins from many structures. It divides into two branches, one of which ends in the pterygoid plexus through the inferior orbital fissure, and the other which ends in the cavernous sinus through the superior orbital fissure.

inferior_petrosal_sinus_left.name: Inferior petrosal sinus (left)
inferior_petrosal_sinus_left.description: The inferior petrosal sinuses are two small sinuses situated on the inferior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone, one on each side. Each inferior petrosal sinus drains the cavernous sinus into the internal jugular vein.

inferior_petrosal_sinus_right.name: Inferior petrosal sinus (right)
inferior_petrosal_sinus_right.description: The inferior petrosal sinuses are two small sinuses situated on the inferior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone, one on each side. Each inferior petrosal sinus drains the cavernous sinus into the internal jugular vein.

inferior_pharyngeal_constrictor_left.name: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor (left)
inferior_pharyngeal_constrictor_left.description: The Inferior pharyngeal constrictor, the thickest of the three constrictors, arises from the sides of the cricoid and thyroid cartilage.

inferior_pharyngeal_constrictor_right.name: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor (right)
inferior_pharyngeal_constrictor_right.description: The Inferior pharyngeal constrictor, the thickest of the three constrictors, arises from the sides of the cricoid and thyroid cartilage.

inferior_rectus_muscle_left.name: Inferior rectus muscle (left)
inferior_rectus_muscle_left.description: The inferior rectus muscle is a muscle in the orbit near the eye. It is one of the four recti muscles in the group of extraocular muscles. It originates from the common tendinous ring, and inserts into the anteroinferior surface of the eye. It depresses the eye (downwards).

inferior_rectus_muscle_right.name: Inferior rectus muscle (right)
inferior_rectus_muscle_right.description: The inferior rectus muscle is a muscle in the orbit near the eye. It is one of the four recti muscles in the group of extraocular muscles. It originates from the common tendinous ring, and inserts into the anteroinferior surface of the eye. It depresses the eye (downwards).

inferior_sagittal_sinus.name: Inferior sagittal sinus
inferior_sagittal_sinus.description: The inferior sagittal sinus (also known as inferior longitudinal sinus), within the human head, is an area beneath the brain which allows blood to drain outwards posteriorly from the center of the head. It drains (from the center of the brain) to the straight sinus (at the back of the head), which connects to the transverse sinuses.

inferior_salivatory_nucleus_left.name: Inferior salivatory nucleus (left)
inferior_salivatory_nucleus_left.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands. They are located in the pontine tegmentum in the brainstem. They both are examples of cranial nerve nuclei.

inferior_salivatory_nucleus_right.name: Inferior salivatory nucleus (right)
inferior_salivatory_nucleus_right.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands. They are located in the pontine tegmentum in the brainstem. They both are examples of cranial nerve nuclei.

inferior_tarsus_left.name: Inferior tarsus (left)
inferior_tarsus_left.description: The tarsi (tarsal plates) are two comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue, about 10 mm (0.39 in) in length for the upper eyelid and 5 mm for the lower eyelid; one is found in each eyelid, and contributes to its form and support. They are located directly above the lid margins.

inferior_tarsus_right.name: Inferior tarsus (right)
inferior_tarsus_right.description: The tarsi (tarsal plates) are two comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue, about 10 mm (0.39 in) in length for the upper eyelid and 5 mm for the lower eyelid; one is found in each eyelid, and contributes to its form and support. They are located directly above the lid margins.

inferior_temporal_gyrus_left.name: Inferior temporal gyrus (left)
inferior_temporal_gyrus_left.description: The inferior temporal gyrus is one of three gyri of the temporal lobe and is located below the middle temporal gyrus, connected behind with the inferior occipital gyrus; it also extends around the infero-lateral border on to the inferior surface of the temporal lobe, where it is limited by the inferior sulcus.

inferior_temporal_gyrus_right.name: Inferior temporal gyrus (right)
inferior_temporal_gyrus_right.description: The inferior temporal gyrus is one of three gyri of the temporal lobe and is located below the middle temporal gyrus, connected behind with the inferior occipital gyrus; it also extends around the infero-lateral border on to the inferior surface of the temporal lobe, where it is limited by the inferior sulcus.

inferior_temporal_sulcus_left.name: Inferior temporal sulcus (left)
inferior_temporal_sulcus_left.description: The inferior surface of the temporal lobe is concave, and is continuous posteriorly with the tentorial surface of the occipital lobe. It is traversed by the inferior temporal sulcus, which extends from near the occipital pole behind, to within a short distance of the temporal pole in front, but is frequently subdivided by bridging gyri.

inferior_temporal_sulcus_right.name: Inferior temporal sulcus (right)
inferior_temporal_sulcus_right.description: The inferior surface of the temporal lobe is concave, and is continuous posteriorly with the tentorial surface of the occipital lobe. It is traversed by the inferior temporal sulcus, which extends from near the occipital pole behind, to within a short distance of the temporal pole in front, but is frequently subdivided by bridging gyri.

infra_orbital_artery_left.name: Infra-orbital artery (left)
infra_orbital_artery_left.description: The infraorbital artery is an artery in the head that branches off the maxillary artery, emerging through the infraorbital foramen, just under the orbit of the eye.

infra_orbital_artery_right.name: Infra-orbital artery (right)
infra_orbital_artery_right.description: The infraorbital artery is an artery in the head that branches off the maxillary artery, emerging through the infraorbital foramen, just under the orbit of the eye.

insula_subcentral_gyrus_and_ant_and_post.name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (left)
insula_subcentral_gyrus_and_ant_and_post.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

insula_subcentral_gyrus_and_ant_and_post.name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (right)
insula_subcentral_gyrus_and_ant_and_post.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

insular_branches_of_middle_cerebral_arte.name: Insular branches of middle cerebral artery (M2) (right)
Insular branches of middle cerebral artery (M2-segment) (left)

intermediate_tendon_of_digastric_muscle_.name: Intermediate tendon of digastric muscle (left)
intermediate_tendon_of_digastric_muscle_.description: The two bellies end in an intermediate tendon which perforates the stylohyoideus muscle, and is held in connection with the side of the body and the greater cornu of the hyoid bone by a fibrous loop, which is sometimes lined by a mucous sheath. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digastric_muscle#Intermediate_tendon

intermediate_tendon_of_digastric_muscle_.name: Intermediate tendon of digastric muscle (right)
intermediate_tendon_of_digastric_muscle_.description: The two bellies end in an intermediate tendon which perforates the stylohyoideus muscle, and is held in connection with the side of the body and the greater cornu of the hyoid bone by a fibrous loop, which is sometimes lined by a mucous sheath. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digastric_muscle#Intermediate_tendon

internal_carotid_artery_left.name: Internal carotid artery (left)
internal_carotid_artery_left.description: The internal carotid artery (Latin: arteria carotis interna) is located in the inner side of the neck in contrast to the external carotid artery.

internal_carotid_artery_right.name: Internal carotid artery (right)
internal_carotid_artery_right.description: The internal carotid artery (Latin: arteria carotis interna) is located in the inner side of the neck in contrast to the external carotid artery.

internal_jugular_vein_left.name: Internal jugular vein (left)
internal_jugular_vein_left.description: The internal jugular vein is a paired jugular vein that collects blood from the brain and the superficial parts of the face and neck. This vein runs in the carotid sheath with the common carotid artery and vagus nerve. It begins in the posterior compartment of the jugular foramen, at the base of the skull.

internal_jugular_vein_right.name: Internal jugular vein (right)
internal_jugular_vein_right.description: The internal jugular vein is a paired jugular vein that collects blood from the brain and the superficial parts of the face and neck. This vein runs in the carotid sheath with the common carotid artery and vagus nerve. It begins in the posterior compartment of the jugular foramen, at the base of the skull.

interpeduncular_fossa_left.name: Interpeduncular fossa (left)
interpeduncular_fossa_left.description: The interpeduncular fossa is a somewhat rhomboid-shaped area of the base of the brain, limited in front by the optic chiasma, behind by the antero-superior surface of the pons, antero-laterally by the converging optic tracts, and postero-laterally by the diverging cerebral peduncles.

interpeduncular_fossa_right.name: Interpeduncular fossa (right)
interpeduncular_fossa_right.description: The interpeduncular fossa is a somewhat rhomboid-shaped area of the base of the brain, limited in front by the optic chiasma, behind by the antero-superior surface of the pons, antero-laterally by the converging optic tracts, and postero-laterally by the diverging cerebral peduncles.

interspinales_colli_muscles_left.name: Interspinales colli muscles (left)
interspinales_colli_muscles_left.description: In the cervical region the cervical interspinales (interspinales colli muscles) are most distinct, and consist of six pairs, the first being situated between the axis and third vertebra, and the last between the seventh cervical and the first thoracic. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interspinales_muscles

interspinales_colli_muscles_right.name: Interspinales colli muscles (right)
interspinales_colli_muscles_right.description: In the cervical region the cervical interspinales (interspinales colli muscles) are most distinct, and consist of six pairs, the first being situated between the axis and third vertebra, and the last between the seventh cervical and the first thoracic. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interspinales_muscles

intertragic_incisure_left.name: Intertragic incisure (left)
intertragic_incisure_left.description: Notch between the tragus and the antitragus.

intertragic_incisure_right.name: Intertragic incisure (right)
intertragic_incisure_right.description: Notch between the tragus and the antitragus.

intervertebral_disc_c2_c3.name: Intervertebral disc C2-C3
intervertebral_disc_c2_c3.description: An intervertebral disc (or intervertebral fibrocartilage) lies between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column. Each disc forms a fibrocartilaginous joint (a symphysis), to allow slight movement of the vertebrae, to act as a ligament to hold the vertebrae together, and to function as a shock absorber for the spine.

intervertebral_disc_c3_c4.name: Intervertebral disc C3-C4
intervertebral_disc_c3_c4.description: An intervertebral disc (or intervertebral fibrocartilage) lies between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column. Each disc forms a fibrocartilaginous joint (a symphysis), to allow slight movement of the vertebrae, to act as a ligament to hold the vertebrae together, and to function as a shock absorber for the spine.

intervertebral_disc_c4_c5.name: Intervertebral disc C4-C5
intervertebral_disc_c4_c5.description: An intervertebral disc (or intervertebral fibrocartilage) lies between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column. Each disc forms a fibrocartilaginous joint (a symphysis), to allow slight movement of the vertebrae, to act as a ligament to hold the vertebrae together, and to function as a shock absorber for the spine.

intraparietal_sulcus_left.name: Intraparietal sulcus (left)
intraparietal_sulcus_left.description: The intraparietal sulcus (IPS) is located on the lateral surface of the parietal lobe, and consists of an oblique and a horizontal portion. The IPS contains a series of functionally distinct subregions that have been intensively investigated using both single cell neurophysiology in primates and human functional neuroimaging.

intraparietal_sulcus_right.name: Intraparietal sulcus (right)
intraparietal_sulcus_right.description: The intraparietal sulcus (IPS) is located on the lateral surface of the parietal lobe, and consists of an oblique and a horizontal portion. The IPS contains a series of functionally distinct subregions that have been intensively investigated using both single cell neurophysiology in primates and human functional neuroimaging.

iris_left.name: Iris (left)
