tuber_of_vermis.name: Tuber of vermis
tuber_of_vermis.description: The tuber of vermis, the most posterior division of the inferior vermis, is of small size, and laterally spreads out into the large inferior semilunar lobules, which comprise at least two-thirds of the inferior surface of the hemisphere.

upper_canine_left.name: Upper canine (left)
upper_canine_left.description: In mammalian oral anatomy, the canine teeth, also called cuspids, dog teeth, or (in the context of the upper jaw) fangs, eye teeth, vampire teeth, or vampire fangs, are the relatively long, pointed teeth. They can appear more flattened however, causing them to resemble incisors and leading them to be called incisiform.

upper_first_molar_tooth_left.name: Upper first molar tooth (left)
upper_first_molar_tooth_left.description: The molars or molar teeth are large, flat teeth at the back of the mouth. They are more developed in mammals. They are used primarily to grind food during chewing. The name molar derives from Latin, molaris dens, meaning "millstone tooth", from mola, millstone and dens, tooth.

upper_first_premolar_left.name: Upper first premolar (left)

upper_lateral_incisor_left.description: Incisors (from Latin incidere, "to cut") are the front teeth present in most mammals. They are located in the premaxilla above and on the mandible below. Humans have a total of eight (two on each side, top and bottom). Opossums have 18, whereas armadillos have none.

uvula_of_palate.name: Uvula of palate
uvula_of_palate.description: The palatine uvula, usually referred to as simply the uvula, is a conic projection from the back edge of the middle of the soft palate, composed of connective tissue containing a number of racemose glands, and some muscular fibers. It also contains many serous glands, which produce thin saliva.

vertebra_c3.name: Vertebra C3
vertebra_c3.description: In tetrapods, cervical vertebrae (singular: vertebra) are the vertebrae of the neck, immediately below the skull. Truncal vertebrae (divided into thoracic and lumbar vertebrae in mammals) lie caudal (toward the tail) of cervical vertebrae. In sauropsid species, the cervical vertebrae bear cervical ribs.

vertebral_artery_left.name: Vertebral artery (left)
vertebral_artery_left.description: The vertebral arteries are major arteries of the neck. Typically, the vertebral arteries originate from the subclavian arteries. Each vessel courses superiorly along each side of the neck, merging within the skull to form the single, midline basilar artery.

vertebral_artery_right.name: Vertebral artery (right)

vertebral_vein_left.name: Vertebral vein (left)
vertebral_vein_left.description: The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas.

vertebral_vein_right.name: Vertebral vein (right)
vertebral_vein_right.description: The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas.

vestibular_nuclei_left.name: Vestibular nuclei (left)
vestibular_nuclei_left.description: The vestibular nuclei (VN) are the cranial nuclei for the vestibular nerve located in the brainstem. In Terminologia Anatomica they are grouped in both the pons and the medulla in the brainstem.

vestibular_nuclei_right.name: Vestibular nuclei (right)
vestibular_nuclei_right.description: The vestibular nuclei (VN) are the cranial nuclei for the vestibular nerve located in the brainstem. In Terminologia Anatomica they are grouped in both the pons and the medulla in the brainstem.

vitreous_body_left.name: Vitreous body (left)
vitreous_body_left.description: The vitreous body (vitreous meaning "glass-like", from Latin vitreus, equivalent to vitr(um) glass + -eus -ous) is the clear gel that fills the space between the lens and the retina of the eyeball (the vitreous chamber) in humans and other vertebrates.

vitreous_body_right.name: Vitreous body (right)

vomer.name: Vomer
vomer.description: The vomer is one of the unpaired facial bones of the skull. It is located in the midsagittal line, and articulates with the sphenoid, the ethmoid, the left and right palatine bones, and the left and right maxillary bones.

white_matter_of_telencephalon_left.name: White matter of telencephalon (left)
white_matter_of_telencephalon_left.description: White matter refers to areas of the central nervous system (CNS) that are mainly made up of myelinated axons, also called tracts.

white_matter_of_telencephalon_right.name: White matter of telencephalon (right)
white_matter_of_telencephalon_right.description: White matter refers to areas of the central nervous system (CNS) that are mainly made up of myelinated axons, also called tracts.

zygomatic_bone_left.name: Zygomatic bone (left)
zygomatic_bone_left.description: In the human skull, the zygomatic bone (cheekbone or malar bone) is a paired irregular bone which articulates with the maxilla, the temporal bone, the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone.

zygomatic_bone_right.name: Zygomatic bone (right)
zygomatic_bone_right.description: In the human skull, the zygomatic bone (cheekbone or malar bone) is a paired irregular bone which articulates with the maxilla, the temporal bone, the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone.

zygomatic_region_left.name: Zygomatic region (left)
zygomatic_region_left.description: Above the buccal region and the parotid region. It corresponds to the zygomatic bone and the zygomatic arch.

zygomatic_region_right.name: Zygomatic region (right)
zygomatic_region_right.description: Above the buccal region and the parotid region. It corresponds to the zygomatic bone and the zygomatic arch.

zygomaticus_major_muscle_left.name: Zygomaticus major muscle (left)
zygomaticus_major_muscle_left.description: The zygomaticus major muscle is a muscle of the human body. It extends from each zygomatic arch (cheekbone) to the corners of the mouth. It is a muscle of facial expression which draws the angle of the mouth superiorly and posteriorly to allow one to smile. Bifid zygomaticus major muscle is a notable variant, and may cause cheek dimples.

zygomaticus_minor_muscle_left.name: Zygomaticus minor muscle (left)
zygomaticus_minor_muscle_left.description: The zygomaticus minor muscle is a muscle of facial expression. It originates from the zygomatic bone, lateral to the rest of the levator labii superioris muscle, and inserts into the outer part of the upper lip. It draws the upper lip backward, upward, and outward and is used in smiling. It is innervated by the facial nerve (VII).
